extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare payment analysts, LTCH and acute care hospital financial officers, health policy stakeholders, and commenters to CMS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed CMS rule establishing FY2027 payment policies, updates, and program requirements for the Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) and Long-Term Care Hospital Prospective Payment System (LTCH PPS), plus related demonstration models and quality programs. Intended for hospitals and stakeholders affected by Medicare inpatient payment policy and for participants in notice-and-comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPPS comparable amount: applicable operating Medicare DSH payment amount
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, the calculation of the “IPPS comparable amount” under §412.529 would include an applicable operating Medicare DSH payment amount that is equal to 73.75 percent of the operating Medicare DSH payment amount that would have been paid based on the statutory Medicare DSH payment formula absent the amendments made by the Affordable Care Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more recent data became available, CMS would use that data to determine the applicable operating Medicare DSH payment amount used to calculate the “IPPS comparable amount” in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH PPS wage index and labor-related share adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.525(c), the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate is adjusted to account for differences in area wages by multiplying the labor-related share of the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate for a case by the applicable LTCH PPS wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: multiply the unadjusted LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate by the proposed labor-related share (73.0 percent) and the proposed wage index value, add the nonlabor-related portion (27.0 percent; adjusted for cost of living if applicable), then multiply by the MS-LTC-DRG relative weight to determine the total adjusted proposed Federal prospective payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH PPS COLA adjustments for Alaska and Hawaii
rubrics_metrics.description: The LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate is adjusted to account for the higher costs of LTCHs located in Alaska and Hawaii by the applicable COLA factors in accordance with §412.525(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed FY2027 COLA factors are shown in the chart in section V.C. of the Addendum and applied to the nonlabor-related portion where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate for FY2027
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed to establish an LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate for FY 2027 of $52,177.04.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This unadjusted standard Federal payment rate is the base used in wage-index and DRG-relative-weight calculations (see example calculation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and availability of IPPS/LTCH tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Most IPPS and LTCH PPS tables referenced in the preamble and Addendum will not be published in the Federal Register in the annual proposed and final rules and will instead be available on the CMS website; exceptions (IPPS Tables 1A–1D and LTCH PPS Table 1E) will be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS lists specific tables (Table 2, Table 3, Table 5, Table 6 series, Table 8A/B, Table 10, Table 15, Table 16, Table 18, LTCH Tables 8C, 11, 12A, 12B, etc.) and provides web navigation instructions and a contact for access problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: New technology add-on payment eligibility (§412.87)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for new technology add-on payments are reviewed based on the eligibility criteria at 42 CFR 412.87. For FY 2028 and subsequent fiscal years CMS proposes to evaluate whether the technology is new and not substantially similar to an existing technology, and that it meets the requirements under §412.87(b) that it represent an advance that substantially improves, relative to technologies previously available, the diagnosis or treatment of Medicare beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposal would be effective beginning with FY 2028 new technology add-on payment applications; no impact for FY 2027. If applications (including Breakthrough Devices, QIDPs, LPADs) would have been approved under current alternative pathway criteria but do not meet the new-not-substantially-similar and §412.87(b) requirements, the proposal could result in savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPPS device pass-through application criteria (§419.66(c)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes that applications received for OPPS device pass-through payment on or after October 1, 2026 must demonstrate that the technology meets the requirements currently reflected at §419.66(c)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns OPPS pass-through application evidentiary expectations with the proposed stricter evaluation for new technology add-on payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable percentage increase to the IPPS standardized amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed update to the national standardized amount for inpatient hospital operating costs by an applicable percentage increase of 2.4 percent (a proposed 3.2 percent market basket percentage increase with a proposed reduction of 0.8 percentage point for the productivity adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospital-specific rates would be updated by the applicable percentage increase (including market basket and productivity adjustment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reductions to applicable percentage increase for failure to submit quality data or meaningful EHR use
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection (d) hospitals that do not submit quality information but are meaningful EHR users would receive a proposed applicable percentage increase of 1.6 percent (reflects a one-quarter percent reduction). Hospitals that are not meaningful EHR users but do submit quality information would receive 0 percent (reflects a three-quarter percent reduction). Hospitals that are not meaningful EHR users and also do not submit quality data would receive -0.8 percent (reflects both reductions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reductions reflect statutory linkages between quality/EHR submission requirements and the annual applicable percentage increase per section 1886(b)(3)(B) of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional exception for discontinuation of low wage index hospital policy
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to extend the transitional exception for low wage index hospitals significantly impacted by the discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy for FY 2027 and subsequent years, using authority under section 1886(d)(5)(I)(i) of the Act, and to exercise that authority in a budget neutral manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: FY 2025 and FY 2026 transition exceptions were set (FY2025: additional amount equal to difference if FY2025 wage index = 95% of FY2024; FY2026: difference if FY2026 wage index = 90.25% of FY2024). The proposal would adopt a narrow transitional exception similar to FY 2026 and apply budget neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 uncompensated care payment methodology: 3-year averaging of Worksheet S-10
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with FY 2025 CMS adopted a multiyear averaging methodology to determine Factor 3 of the uncompensated care payment methodology using a 3-year average of audited data on uncompensated care costs from Worksheet S-10 for the 3 most recent fiscal years for which audited data are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 CMS proposes to use a 3-year average of audited data from the FY 2021, FY 2022, and FY 2023 cost reports to calculate Factor 3 for all eligible hospitals; this method mitigates large year-to-year fluctuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental payment methodology for IHS, Tribal hospitals, and Puerto Rico
rubrics_metrics.description: Since FY 2023 CMS established a supplemental payment for IHS and Tribal hospitals and hospitals located in Puerto Rico and summarizes the ongoing methodology for supplemental payments in section IV.D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will continue the methodology outlined for supplemental payments for these entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCH and FCHIP demonstration budget neutrality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) demonstration and Rural Community Hospital (RCH) demonstration are authorized to be budget neutral; the authorizing legislation requires FCHIP to be budget neutral and RCH effects were previously made budget neutral as required under section 410A(c)(2) of Public Law 108-173.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the FCHIP extension period, CMS proposes to continue the budget neutrality approach used in the demonstration initial period—to offset payments across CAHs nationally—should the demonstration incur costs to Medicare. For RCH, CMS is not proposing a FY2027 budget neutrality offset and proposes to apply offsets in FY2028 rulemaking once estimated costs are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH PPS proposed update and quality reporting penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed annual market basket update to the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate of 2.4 percent for FY 2027 (3.2 percent market basket increase minus 0.8 productivity adjustment). LTCHs that failed to submit quality data as required by 1886(m)(5)(A)(i) would receive a proposed update of 0.4 percent, reflecting a 2.0 percentage point reduction for failure to submit quality data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns LTCH update and penalties with statutory quality reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program reporting requirement and linkage to payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(b)(3)(B)(viii) requires subsection (d) hospitals to report data in accordance with the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program for purposes of measuring and making publicly available information on health care quality and links the quality data submission to the annual applicable percentage increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to report quality data affects hospitals' applicable percentage increase as described elsewhere in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful use of certified EHR technology requirement and linkage to payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1886(b)(3)(B)(ix), 1886(n), and 1814(l) require eligible hospitals and CAHs to demonstrate they are meaningful users of certified EHR technology to improve the quality of health care and link submission of information demonstrating meaningful use to the annual applicable percentage increase for eligible hospitals and the applicable percent for CAHs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals that do not meet meaningful EHR use requirements face reductions (see reductions entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH Quality Reporting Program penalty avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(m)(5) requires each LTCH to submit quality measure data in accordance with the Long Term Care Hospital Quality Reporting Program and to avoid a 2-percentage point reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit appropriate quality data results in a 2-percentage point reduction to LTCH updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Value-Based Purchasing (VBP) Program objectives and payment linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(o) requires the Secretary to establish a VBP program under which value-based incentive payments are made in a fiscal year to hospitals that meet the performance standards established on an announced set of quality and efficiency measures. Purposes include measuring quality of hospital inpatient care, linking measure performance to payment, and making publicly available information on hospital quality of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VBP ties publicly reported measure performance to incentive payments and payment adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Acquired Condition (HAC) Reduction Program penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(p) requires a reduction in payment for subsection (d) hospitals that rank in the worst-performing 25 percent with respect to measures of hospital-acquired conditions for the purpose of measuring HACs, linking measure performance to payment, and making publicly available information on health care quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals in the worst-performing quartile receive payment reductions under the HAC Reduction Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(q) requires a reduction in payment for subsection (d) hospitals for excess readmissions based on measures for applicable conditions under the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program for the purpose of measuring readmissions, linking measure performance to payment, and making publicly available information on health care quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess readmissions for specified conditions can trigger payment reductions per statutory methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPS-exempt cancer hospitals (PCHs) quality reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1866(k) applies to PPS-exempt cancer hospitals and requires PCHs to report data in accordance with the PCH Quality Reporting Program for purposes of measuring and making publicly available information on the quality of care furnished by PCHs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no reduction in payment to a PCH that does not report data (unlike IPPS hospitals).

rubrics_metrics.name: 1115A demonstration testing standard (TEAM and CJR-X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1115A authorizes testing of innovative payment and service delivery models that preserve or enhance quality of care while reducing program expenditures; TEAM and the proposed CJR-X model are to be tested under this authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should maintain or improve quality while reducing costs; CMS solicits comments and may update policies via notice-and-comment rulemaking. TEAM bundles payment for episodes and holds participants accountable for spending and quality; CJR-X would hold acute care hospitals accountable for LEJR episodes and 90-day post-discharge performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare reimbursement of non-renal organ acquisition costs and reasonable cost principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to make payment and policy changes to ensure Medicare reimburses non-renal organ acquisition costs to IOPOs and HCLs on a reasonable cost basis and to clarify, revise, and/or codify Medicare's reasonable cost payment policies related to allowable costs and overhead allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes are intended to increase compliance with reasonable cost principles, increase payment accuracy, and improve provider understanding; also includes codifying appeals policy provisions for IOPOs and HCLs for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) and significance under Executive Order 12866
rubrics_metrics.description: A RIA must be prepared for a regulatory action that is significant under section 3(f)(1) of E.O. 12866. Section 3(f) defines a “significant regulatory action” if it is likely to: (1) have an annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more or otherwise materially affect the economy; (2) create a serious inconsistency with another agency; (3) materially alter budgetary impact of entitlements/grants/user fees; or (4) raise novel legal or policy issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB has determined this rulemaking is significant per section 3(f)(1) and has reviewed the regulations; CMS prepared a RIA presenting costs and benefits to the best of its ability. The RIA should estimate redistributional and aggregate impacts (CMS estimates > $100 million redistribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the IPPS and LTCH PPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary objective is to create incentives for hospitals to operate efficiently and minimize unnecessary costs while ensuring payments are sufficient to adequately compensate hospitals for their legitimate costs in delivering necessary care to Medicare beneficiaries and to preserve the Medicare Hospital Insurance Trust Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed changes (rate updates, add-on payments, program proposals) are assessed against these objectives with an expectation that they yield reasonable, equitable outcomes while avoiding or minimizing unintended adverse consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and methodology of CMS quantitative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS's quantitative analysis presents projected effects of proposed policy changes by estimating payments per case while holding all other payment policies constant and includes limitations (e.g., estimates do not reflect changes in hospital admissions or real case-mix intensity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are referred to the specific sections for detailed impact analysis; estimates include operating payment impacts, capital payments, and are used to determine whether the rule is significant under E.O. 12866.
